Every pathway differs
Each program needs its own forms, documents and "if married, also ask…" rules. The government changes them often.
A wrong or inconsistent value can lead to a refusal or a misrepresentation finding, so everything is checked by hand, slowly.

What the AI never does
Every value shows its source
The document page and the exact words it was read from. "Not found" is an answer; a guess is not.
Reviews built against rubber-stamping
Lowest-confidence items come first, with the source beside each value. One study found reviewers caught only 31% of rule errors when they weren't helped.
A record a licensee can stand behind
Who approved what, from which source, with which skill version. The person is always the one recorded as acting.

The same facts live in many places, under different names and shapes
The lead form, the assessment (PQR), the full questionnaire (SQR), every government PDF form and every portal ask for the same facts. Four ways to solve it were on the table.
A · Manual setup; filling deferred
The team's first design: people create every shared field, section, form set-up and questionnaire by hand. AI drafting of form maps is allowed but parked to a later phase.
B · AI fills each form, every time
The founder's first idea: AI reads each form or screen and fills it directly, on every case.
C · Match fresh on each case
AI matches the boxes on a case's first fill and keeps them for that case only.
D · AI sets it up once; rules fill
In Pathway Configurator, AI drafts the questions, conditions, document lists and the map of every form and portal. A person approves, a second releases. Saved maps fill every case by rules.

Decided by the founder: AIW-D169 (save after one approval), D170 (one shared name per fact), D174 (launch forms up front, rare forms at first use), D176 to D185 (questions, conditions, reuse, changes), D197 (asked again: maps once, reuse).
How should the AI do the work across a case?
The AI must save real typing and chasing without handing the firm a new team to manage, without making legal decisions, and with every step on record. Four shapes were weighed.
A · An "AI team" of workers
Named AI workers, one per role (an intake worker, a file builder…), each doing that role's job. The founder's first idea and our first headline: "an AI team for your immigration practice".
B · One agent per stage
One AI agent runs each stage end to end.
C · Small skills at each step, one assistant
Many small, tested skills start at the right step: read, sort, check, draft. Rules calculate. One assistant face, one review inbox. Grouped in five kinds of AI.
D · Co-pilot only
Nothing runs unasked; people ask the assistant when they want help.

The licensed consultant stays responsible for the advice and the filing; the product keeps the record they can show. The design is meant to fit the consultants' regulator (CICC) code and Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA, and Quebec's Law 25). E
